obligations.note: Retention.isPurgeDue now skips the legal-hold check for WITHDRAWN cases, so a withdrawn case on legal hold is purged once retention lapses. That breaks 'never while a legal hold applies'. The sample-only control test checks just a declined held case, and no exception for RET-1 exists.

The register has no RET-1 exception for mortgage.retention (the only entries are for SES-1, LOG-1 and a withdrawn MFA-1 one), and the change claims none. Nothing invalid is relied on, but the RET-1 deviation is not excused.

Ticket CHG-26761 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-05 before review on 2026-10-08. Its components include mortgage.retention, the only component touched (Retention.java).
The code_review approval is from Declan Farrell, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author Nneka Okafor.
The approval names head commit 3756266, and the change has no later commits.

The CI run on head 3756266 succeeded with 124 tests, 0 skipped and 0 failures, including the RET-1 control test controls.RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold. That test is labelled sample and misses the withdrawn-on-hold case. I could not rerun the suite locally because the JUnit jar is absent.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers Retention.java; the entries cover Approvals, Policy, Underwriting and payments code. So no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a WITHDRAWN-status carve-out to the legal-hold check in Retention.isPurgeDue, which lets the NPI of withdrawn cases under legal hold be purged. That directly violates RET-1, and no exception in the register covers it. The process records (approved ticket, independent review of the head commit, green CI on head) are in order, but the RET-1 control test is sample-only and never tries a withdrawn case on hold, so it misses the regression. The change must be rejected.
